front: Why society is encouraged to reduce waste
back: 90% of waste is dumped or burned, mostly in low income countries; poorly managed waste pollutes oceans, blocks drains, causes flooding, spreads disease and harms wildlife.
Putting materials, components and products back into good use at the end of their life, again and again, so fewer new materials are needed.
Solving problems while minimising environmental damage — without creating other problems.
Creating goods and services that meet user needs while reducing ecological impact and resource depletion.
A measurement of a product's environmental impact from cradle to grave.
Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Repair, Rethink and Refuse.
Designing a product to last only for a set time so newer versions can replace it.
Designing a product so its materials are put to good use in a new product at the end of its life.

front: How much global waste is recycled?
back: Only about 13.5% of global waste is recycled and 5.5% is composted. Low income countries recycle only about 4%.
An arrangement helping producers in developing countries trade with other countries, improving trading conditions and workers' rights.

front: Ways to live in a greener world
back: Reduce food waste, packaging and plastics; recycle correctly; repair rather than upgrade; use green energy; travel greener; use eco settings and turn off lights at home.

front: Average life of a mobile phone
back: About two and a half years, or 15–18 months for a smartphone.
Releasing new models frequently with small improvements, which helps ensure consistent sales — common with mobile phones.
PV cells (solar) as power supplies or trickle chargers, and wind-up technology that needs no batteries.
